subject: 9mmhandgun
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: 9mmhandgun, in the place of the game's models/v_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/p_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/w_9mmhandgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_grenade.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, A, D, D where the asset was B, D, A, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Reads as a 9mm pistol in every view: a long slide with a muzzle bore at one end, a grip plate at the other, and a trigger guard. Lying on its side as the brief asks, the grip runs out sideways (top and below views). The grip is a fairly blocky slab, but the outline is not clearly off.

M2.reason: Measured size 9.5 x 1.9 x 9.7 units against the brief's 10 long: 2.8% off, within 15%. Length is 5% short, which is close to the ask.

M3.reason: Present and legible: slide serrations at the rear (top and right views), a trigger guard loop (top and below views), a muzzle bore (back view), and a grip with a base plate. Not legible at this scale: the trigger itself and the front and rear sights. A small block at the muzzle (front view) may be the front sight, but I cannot confirm the rear sight or trigger in any view. A pistol's small parts are not confirmed, so M3 is held at 1.

M4.reason: Black grip and dark slide bands over grey steel, matching the brief's 'black and grey polymer and steel'. The grip reads as dark polymer, the slide as grey metal, in the first-person, in-hand and lineup views.

M5.reason: The slide's metal texture is streaked and blurred (sides, front-left, top), coarser than Half-Life's crisp weapon surfaces. The grip's noise texture is flat. The serrations and muzzle are there, but the surface detail is softer than a Valve pistol's.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the line-up at the game's size, the asset (A) was passed off as a Valve model: judges picked Valve's own models over it on every reading.

M7.reason: Lies on its side on the floor as the brief says: the grip extends sideways, the muzzle is the front, and the top is upright. No fault in orientation is visible in the six views.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. 88 triangles, well under twice the median of 142 for Half-Life's own weapons. No open, inside-out or floating parts visible in the views.

W1.reason: In the first-person view the asset sits where the game's own gun sits, at the same angle, held in the right hand, the same way round. Through the 14-frame attack the gun stays with the hand in every frame, with no visible detachment, though the frames are small.
